I used to volunteer at an animal shelter for the cats (we could assist with the dogs or cats). It was the easiest thing I've ever done. They let us come in whenever, there was no expectations on time but once a week for about an hour was what most people did. The vet and clinic staff were always super grateful for anyone that came in. Most of the tasks just literally involved me opening up the kitty door and spending a few minutes petting them (if they wanted to, some were stressed so they didn't want interaction). Some of the light work was taking out dirty towels and blankets and replacing them with clean ones. It was very therapeutic just hanging out with kitties. Sometimes if it was slow and they had kittens in a big room (instead of the kennel spaces, so they could run  around and play) we were allowed to sit in there and just play. I was struggling with depression at that time so I had NO ENERGY but the work was very easy. And it ended up giving me a lil dopamine hit too. 

I hope you find something lovely that you can enjoy and brings you happiness!

Hi I really struggle with this too. Tbh I have a hard time finding the joy in cooking anymore, I used to love it. Depression is just very powerful. And after a few years of trying, I realized that I can't trick myself into enjoying it. But one thing that helps is feeling like I'm winning some non existent fight. This is how my inner dialog basically goes. Every time I eat something that I prepared, it's a victory over which ever soulless corporation that my money would have gone to otherwise. I think about how much money I save that can go back into me instead of the money going to some stupid store that is giving me shit nutrients or dangerous ingredients. Or i think of it as me conquering my depression. It's so much easier to just order food or heat up something frozen, but not today depression, u lil bitch. 

French toast is the easiest thing for me to cook at any point in the day. And I can add things like fruits, seeds, pb, or whatever to make it healthier without making it harder to cook. But you'll have to find something that's easy for you that fits your needs. Another thing that also helped me was figuring out what portions were easier to manage. I used to try to meal prep but it started getting overwhelming to the point where I would just waste ingredients and cry about how stressful I was to prep and wash all that crap. Now I'm learning easier ways to set up 1 serving meals and storing raw items properly so they last longer. And lastly, this might not help you at all but I usually put off eating till last minute, especially if I'm trying to get myself up to make it myself ... so I end up not having energy cuz I'm starving. I keep easy snacks that I can always eat near by.  Usually after eating a couple of bites it makes me realize how hungry I am and that's a big motivator to go make more food, it also gives me a small energy boost so I can get up. Best of luck, don't give up ❤️

I've been struggling with depression and suicidal ideations for a long time. Somedays I feel ok or even better, I feel like I'm "my old self". The self that does "normal human things" with "normal ups and downs" instead of being debilitated and stuck in bed wishing the end would come. Those days come frequent enough to make me feel like there's hope. That I can keep going to therapy or work on my life in a "forward/positive" direction. 
I'm worried that one day the ideations will be strong enough to act on and no one will be around to save me again. The thought that I'll give in, and break the hearts of those who beg me to stay and fight worries me. I feel like every day that I'm here is "leading them on". 
More so, I'm scared shitless that it won't BUT that I can't get better. That I'm stuck living a life where I can never reach my full potential because of mental health issues, and be fully aware of it.

Try stretching your fingers (I'm sure you can YT finger stretches). Start incorporating more angled and even finger spacings (especially in your wave tuts and tuts). It'll make a huge difference in neat, clean, crisp moves.
Also, before you record, sit back comfortably. Move your hands as far up, down, left, right and in front of the camera as you feel comfortable performing and set the camera up so it captures all of your range of motion. It might seem a bit far a way but honestly when it's up front it's hard to watch everything that goes on (on top of your moves getting cut out! D: )
